issue: The 'DERIVED' box states 'decode bandwidth-bound' as a bare property, while the prose says this is a low-batch regime whose persistence depends on batch size, context precision, kernel, and hardware.
evidence: Figure box 2: 'decode bandwidth-bound'. Page 410: 'sharding distributes the model across the node so decode lands in the bandwidth-bound regime (the low-batch regime of Ch. 8; batch size, context precision, kernel, and hardware decide whether it stays there)'.
acceptance_test: Add the regime qualifier to the box, e.g. 'decode: bandwidth-bound in this low-batch scenario', or add a caption sentence that the box is a scenario-specific derived regime, not a universal property.

issue: The figure asserts as 'FACT' exactly the three quantities the prose explicitly says are NOT facts. Box 1 is headed '1 · FACT' and contains 'request rate ~2 rps', 'utilization 45%', and the baseline TTFT — the same three values the prose labels as assumed scenario inputs that 'become FACTS only once instrumented and recorded in a genuine load test'. Figure and prose therefore assign different evidence classes to the same numbers, which is the book's central provenance discipline.
evidence: Figure box 1: '1 · FACT / request rate ~2 rps / utilization 45% / baseline TTFT … 450 ms'. Prose, printed p. 390: 'These are assumed baseline inputs, not gathered FACTS (R-07): no author-run load test produced them, so they are labeled an assumed baseline for a worked example (an input to the math), not a measured runtime quantity a FACT would be. They become FACTS only once instrumented and recorded in a genuine load test.'
acceptance_test: Either relabel box 1 with the book's own assumption/scenario label from the Ch. 4 taxonomy (e.g. '1 · ASSUMED BASELINE (scenario input)'), or change the prose so the capstone values are presented as instrumented facts. The figure's evidence label and the prose's evidence class for the same three numbers must be identical, and the caption must state which it is.

issue: The caption describes the loop as 'closing on FACT → DERIVED → PATTERN', which omits the return arrow to FACT — the only element that makes this a feedback loop rather than a three-step pipeline. The figure's own subtitle calls it the 'Pattern-Measurement-Feedback Loop', so the caption understates the drawn structure.
evidence: Caption: 'FIGURE 26.2: Pattern Application Diagram: the Pattern-Measurement-Feedback Loop applied to the capstone scenario, closing on FACT → DERIVED → PATTERN.' Drawn arrows: 'trace' (FACT→DERIVED), 'validate' (DERIVED→PATTERN), 'feedback' (PATTERN→FACT).
acceptance_test: Caption reads '…closing the loop FACT → DERIVED → PATTERN → FACT', naming the return edge explicitly.

issue: The return path carries two labels with unclear ownership: 'feedback' on the vertical leg and 'adjust + pick pattern' on the horizontal leg leaving the PATTERN box. A reader can reasonably read 'adjust + pick pattern' as the label of the PATTERN→FACT arrow (i.e. the loop's action) or as a separate step, and the two readings imply different control flow.
evidence: Rendered: red horizontal segment from the PATTERN box's left edge labelled 'adjust + pick pattern'; red vertical segment rising to the FACT box labelled 'feedback'.
acceptance_test: One label per arrow, or an explicit ordering: the PATTERN→FACT arrow carries a single label (e.g. 'feedback: adjust + pick pattern') and the intermediate segment carries no competing text.

issue: Box 2 states 'decode bandwidth-bound' as an unqualified DERIVED result, while the prose treats the regime as conditional on batch size, context precision, kernel, and hardware. The figure is the more quotable artifact, so an unqualified label risks becoming the universal claim the book elsewhere avoids.
evidence: Figure box 2: '2 · DERIVED / decode bandwidth-bound'. Prose, printed p. 390: 'sharding distributes the model across the node so decode lands in the bandwidth-bound regime (the low-batch regime of Ch. 8, batch size, context precision, kernel, and hardware decide whether it stays there)'.
acceptance_test: Box 2 reads 'decode bandwidth-bound (baseline regime; see Ch. 8)' or carries a short qualifier, matching the prose's conditionality.

figure: FIGURES 26.2, A.1, A.2, A.3, A.4 (book-level pattern)
issue: A systematic pattern: each of these figures prints a title inside the figure and then repeats it verbatim as the caption's opening words ('Pattern Application Diagram', 'A conceptual layering of frontier AI systems', 'Where should intelligence live?', 'Shared-depth execution reuses weights, not necessarily history state'). The caption therefore adds no information at the point where the reader needs it, and the reader's eye is asked to read the same sentence twice.
evidence: FIG 26.2 in-figure title 'Pattern Application Diagram' = caption opening; FIG A.2 in-figure title 'A conceptual layering of frontier AI systems' = caption opening; FIG A.3 in-figure title 'Where Should Intelligence Live?' = caption opening; FIG A.4 in-figure heading 'Shared-depth execution reuses weights, not necessarily history state' = caption opening.
acceptance_test: For each figure, either the in-figure title is dropped (caption carries the title) or the caption opens with what the figure shows rather than restating the title; no figure's caption begins with a verbatim copy of its in-figure title.

issue: The subtitle 'vs each model's own predecessor' is not accurate for the GLM-5.3-Flash row, whose stated baseline is GLM-5.3 (the same-generation base model, not a predecessor). The caption correctly generalizes this to 'each model's own stated reference,' so the subtitle over-specifies and is locally inconsistent with the GLM row.
evidence: Subtitle: 'vs each model's own predecessor'. GLM row 'own baseline' column: 'vs GLM-5.3'. Caption: '...each model's vendor-reported ratio of its own stated reference (e.g. DeepSeek V4 vs V3.2)...'
acceptance_test: Change the subtitle to match the caption's wording, e.g. 'vs each model's own stated reference (predecessor or base model)', so the GLM-5.3 baseline is not mislabeled a predecessor.

issue: The table places vendor-reported percentages with different metric scopes in the same 'KV cache*' and 'Compute*' columns, inviting cross-row comparison even though the caption/footnote say the scopes differ.
evidence: Table columns 'KV cache*' and 'Compute*'; GLM row has '~23%' with 'BF16 / layer' and '~33%' with 'attention only per head / layer'; footnote says '*Metric scopes differ'; caption says 'GLM's rows are per-layer/per-head scope, not total FLOPs or total cache'.
acceptance_test: Split the columns by scope (e.g. 'Total KV / total compute' vs 'per-layer/per-head attention') or add an explicit 'Scope' column and visually separate GLM's attention-only values from DeepSeek's total-model values; the reader should not be able to compare 10% and 33% as the same metric.

issue: The metric scope is stated only for the GLM row ('BF16 / layer', 'attention only per head / layer'). The two DeepSeek rows carry no scope annotation, so the reader cannot tell what the denominator of '100% → 7%' and '100% → 10%' is (total KV cache across all layers and heads? per-token? per-layer?). The footnote's '*Metric scopes differ' flags the problem without resolving it, and the caption's 'GLM's rows are per-layer/per-head scope' implies but never states the DeepSeek scope.
evidence: Figure rows: 'DeepSeek V4-Flash … KV cache* 100%→7% / Compute* 100%→10%' (no scope note) vs 'GLM-5.3-Flash … 100%→23% (BF16 / layer) / 100%→33% (attention only per head / layer)'. Footnote: '*Metric scopes differ. 7% remaining = 93% reduction.' Caption: 'GLM's rows are per-layer/per-head scope, not total FLOPs or total cache'.
acceptance_test: Every row states its scope inline (e.g. 'DeepSeek: total KV cache, all layers' / 'total attention FLOPs'), or the figure carries a scope column; the caption's scope sentence covers all three rows, not only GLM.

issue: The caption contains a broken sentence: 'An architect who re-derives them per candidate model would then re-derive the model-specific KV and FLOP constants (…) and under-provisioning.' The clause 'and under-provisioning' is ungrammatical and the intended consequence (that the architect under-provisions) is left unstated.
evidence: Caption: 'An architect who re-derives them per candidate model would then re-derive the model-specific KV and FLOP constants (using a model whose vendor reports 7% KV vs 1M context as if it were 100%) and under-provisioning.'
acceptance_test: Sentence reads, e.g., 'An architect who re-derives them per candidate model would then re-derive the model-specific KV and FLOP constants (using a model whose vendor reports 7% KV vs 1M context as if it were 100%) and would under-provision.'

issue: The caption runs to roughly 200 words across two paragraphs, mixing figure description, provenance rules, a cross-reference to Fig 7.1, a teaching-model statement, and a worked misreading. A caption this long is read as body text and is unlikely to be read at all; the parts that are not caption material should move into the surrounding prose.
evidence: Caption begins 'FIGURE A.1: Vendor-relative KV/compute ratios.' and continues through '…not yet independently reproduced on a serving stack (see A.2).'
acceptance_test: Caption is reduced to what the figure shows (rows, scope, the not-a-ranking caveat, sources); the 'same message as Fig 7.1's CQOA line' and the 'architect who re-derives them' worked misreading move to adjacent body text with a forward reference from the caption.

issue: The smallest annotations ('reported 2026-06', 'reported 2026-08', 'BF16 / layer', 'attention only per head / layer', and the two-line source footnote) render noticeably smaller than the rest of the figure and are at risk of falling below the book's 8 pt print floor. These are not decorative: the dates and the scope notes carry the figure's provenance argument.
evidence: Rendered at 150 dpi: the gray 'reported 2026-06' / 'reported 2026-08' lines and the italic footnote are visibly smaller than the row labels and column headers.
acceptance_test: Print proof at 100% shows every annotation in FIG A.1 at ≥8 pt, including the footnote and scope notes; if any is smaller, raise it or move the content into the caption.

issue: Red is used for two unrelated meanings inside one figure: the 'NOT A CROSS-MODEL PERFORMANCE RANKING' warning callout and the DeepSeek V4-Flash row identity (row label and its two arrows). A reader can associate the warning with that row, or read the row as 'the flagged one'.
evidence: Red-bordered red-text callout 'NOT A CROSS-MODEL PERFORMANCE RANKING'; row label 'DeepSeek V4-Flash' in red with red arrows '100%→7%' and '100%→10%'; the other two rows use blue and green.
acceptance_test: The warning callout uses a neutral treatment (black/gray border and text) or a distinct non-row hue, so no row identity color is reused for a caveat; row identity colors remain consistent across the appendix.

issue: The stacked bars with increasing dates visually encode a chronology/layering that the caption explicitly disclaims ('not a causal lineage', 'a later layer does not require the one below it', 'eras overlap'). The drawing still reads as a sequential stack from Transformer to Agent Fleet.
evidence: Figure: stacked bars 'Transformer ~2017' through 'Agent Fleet ~2026'. Caption: 'the vertical stacking is a layering ... not a causal lineage: a later layer does not require the one below it, and the eras overlap.'
acceptance_test: Redraw as a timeline with overlapping era bands, or as a non-stacked set of era markers; if the stack is retained, add an explicit visual break/annotation that the vertical order is not dependency or chronology, and remove the date column's implication of a single sequence.

figure: FIGURE A.2 — A conceptual layering of frontier AI systems
issue: The legend promises a shade encoding that the figure does not implement: 'darker shade = MoE transition ~2022'. All three efficiency-led bands (Transformer ~2017, Efficient Transformer ~2020, MoE Transformer ~2022) are drawn in the same brown, so the legend's only within-family cue is inert, and the reader cannot locate the 'MoE transition' the legend points at. The legend also shows only one brown swatch, so the ramp is never demonstrated.
evidence: Legend: 'Efficiency-led (dashed) — context / cost / capacity; darker shade = MoE transition ~2022' with a single brown swatch. Bands: 'Transformer ~2017', 'Efficient Transformer ~2020', 'MoE Transformer ~2022' all rendered in the same tan/brown fill.
acceptance_test: The MoE Transformer band is rendered in a visibly darker brown than the two bands above it and the legend shows both shades (or the 'darker shade' clause is deleted); the distinction survives a grayscale conversion.

figure: FIGURE A.2 — A conceptual layering of frontier AI systems
issue: The caption ends with a dangling clause: 'a later layer does not require the one below it, and the era overlap.' The second conjunct has no predicate, so the sentence does not parse. The intended point (that the era markers overlap, so the layering is not a strict succession) is left unstated.
evidence: Caption: '…the vertical stacking is a layering (which capabilities sit on which substrate), not a causal lineage: a later layer does not require the one below it, and the era overlap. Read it as "what exists at each stage" not "what caused what".'
acceptance_test: Caption reads, e.g., '…a later layer does not require the one below it, and the era markers overlap.' — a complete sentence with a predicate.

figure: FIGURE A.2 — A conceptual layering of frontier AI systems
issue: The base 'Transformer ~2017' band is drawn in the efficiency-led (brown, dashed) family, but the base transformer is not an efficiency-led layer; the legend's category label therefore misclassifies the bottom band. The reader is told the brown family means 'context / cost / capacity' and then finds the origin of the stack in it.
evidence: Legend: 'Efficiency-led (dashed) — context / cost / capacity'. Bands: 'Transformer ~2017' (brown, dashed), 'Efficient Transformer ~2020' (brown, dashed), 'MoE Transformer ~2022' (brown, dashed).
acceptance_test: Either the base Transformer band is given its own legend category (e.g. 'Foundation (solid)') or the legend's brown family is renamed to cover it (e.g. 'Model architecture (dashed) — foundation, efficiency, MoE'), so no band contradicts its legend entry.

figure: FIGURE A.2 — A conceptual layering of frontier AI systems
issue: Evidence-label scope mismatch between the figure and its caption: the in-figure subtitle closes with '[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]', while the caption labels the figure only '[ILLUSTRATIVE] conceptual'. The figure therefore claims a derived component that the caption does not acknowledge, leaving the reader unsure which span the DERIVED label binds to.
evidence: In-figure subtitle: 'Selected illustrative mechanism milestones — a non-comprehensive chronology; approximate era markers (≈), not release dates. [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]'. Caption: '…Read it as "what exists at each stage" not "what caused what". [ILLUSTRATIVE] conceptual'.
acceptance_test: The figure's internal label and the caption's label agree, or the caption explicitly splits the span (e.g. '[ILLUSTRATIVE] band structure; [DERIVED] era markers') so the DERIVED label has a stated referent.
